channel.title: Sunward
channel.description: Only good news. Each morning Sunward reads real newsrooms, keeps the stories where something got better, and says why in one line.

item.title: This Blue Whale Population Grew 1,000% Since the End of Antarctic Whaling
item.description: Antarctic blue whales have grown from 418 to about 4,000 since whaling stopped in 1973. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: ‘Huge experiment in biogeography’: US offshore windfarms are creating artificial reefs
item.description: Offshore wind turbine bases off the US coast are becoming reefs that host sea life. Evidence: Early research. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: Scientists ‘Cure’ Deadly Brain Tumors in Every Mouse Tested with New Cancer Therapy
item.description: A new immune cell therapy cleared an aggressive childhood brain tumour in every mouse tested. Evidence: Early research. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: New discovery reveals what may be holding back room-temperature superconductors
item.description: Scientists found electrons can pair at room temperature, a clue for future superconductors. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: What We’re Reading: Phone Bans Are Improving Kids’ Test Scores
item.description: Studies suggest school phone bans are lifting children's test scores. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Keep phones out of the bedroom at night for a week and notice the change. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: Country diary: Thrilling views of Iceland’s humpbacks, (perhaps) lured in by Céline Dion | Claire Stares
item.description: Humpback whale numbers are rising in Iceland's longest fjord. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: 125,000 years ago, hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert
item.description: Finds show early humans lived beside large lakes with hippos in Arabia 125,000 years ago. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Autistic brains look surprisingly similar on average. Then scientists looked closer.
item.description: Brain scans show autistic people differ widely from each other, which may lead to more personal support. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: US homelessness decline hits its steepest one-year drop in a decade
item.description: US homelessness fell over 6% in 2025, about 49,000 fewer people, the steepest drop in a decade. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: April Surac built NeuraSensa so art adapts to the people using it
item.description: A young designer built NeuraSensa so public art adjusts to visitors' sensory needs. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Pakistan's solar revolution is so successful the national grid is lagging behind
item.description: Rooftop solar has lifted solar's share of Pakistan's electricity from 1% to 28%. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: West Coast’s First Ever Sea Turtle Hatchlings Released into the Pacific (LOOK)
item.description: Olive ridley turtle hatchlings from the West Coast's first recorded nest were released into the Pacific. How you can help: Give nesting turtles space on beaches and keep lights off near the shore at night. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: William and Kate celebrate Earthshot Prize winners in Mumbai
item.description: This year's Earthshot Prize winners were celebrated in Mumbai for environmental solutions. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Algeria Returns Kindness Shown by Kansans Who Welcomed its World Cup Team with the Trip of a Lifetime
item.description: Algeria hosted Kansas families on a free trip to thank them for welcoming its World Cup team. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Warren Buffett Gives Away $5.5 Billion in Thanksgiving Gift, Saying Kindness Is Priceless
item.description: Warren Buffett gave about $5.5 billion in shares to charity in his yearly Thanksgiving donation. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Largest Electric Bus Fleet in New York to Serve Bronx Neighborhood Elevated Asthma Rates
item.description: New York's largest electric school bus fleet now runs in a South Bronx area with high child asthma. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Ask your local school board whether electric buses are planned for your district. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Can this experimental orchard save the UK’s cider industry?
item.description: A Somerset orchard is testing apple varieties and methods to keep cider farming going as the climate shifts. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Guardian Environment.

item.title: The Greek coastline cleanup that turned trash into a pollution map
item.description: A cleanup of a Greek islet turned decades of washed-up trash into a map of ocean pollution. How you can help: Join a beach or river cleanup and log what you find. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Animal welfare ballot measures had a strong night in the 2026 midterms
item.description: Voters backed several animal welfare ballot measures by wide margins in the November midterms. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Farmer Finds Unknown Seeds in His Attic – and Grows an Ancient ‘Miracle’ Grain
item.description: An Italian farmer grew an old wheat variety from seeds found in his attic, reviving a lost grain. How you can help: Save seeds from heirloom plants you grow and swap them with neighbours. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: 30% Drop in Levels of Forever Chemicals in England’s Rivers, 49% in Fish – ‘Brilliant to See’
item.description: Two banned forever chemicals have fallen 30% in England's rivers and 49% in fish. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: NASA is offering $1 million for bold ideas to help build a Moon base
item.description: NASA is offering students $1 million for ideas to help build a Moon base. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Tokyo Tackles Trash Troubles with New Generation of Robotic Street Waste Bins
item.description: Tokyo is trying solar compacting bins and trash-hauling robots to keep tourist areas clean. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Carry your litter until you find a bin, as many in Japan already do. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Climbers Lug Endangered and Orphaned Seal Pup Up a Cliff to Safety
item.description: Climbers in Greece carried an orphaned, critically endangered monk seal pup up a cliff to rescuers. How you can help: If you find a lone seal pup, keep back and call a local marine rescue line. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Hidden ecosystem: Scientists discover 245 animals living inside a single deep-sea rock
item.description: Scientists found over 4,100 tiny animals from 245 species living inside deep-sea rock nodules. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Can Barbershops Turn Trust Into Better Health for Black Men?
item.description: Barbershops are offering health checks to Black men in a setting they already trust. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Book a blood pressure check; many pharmacies offer them free. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: An ancient virus may help explain what makes the human brain different
item.description: An ancient virus may help explain how human brains came to develop differently from chimps'. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: This Tourette’s wrist device cut tics by a quarter in a UK trial
item.description: A wrist device cut tics by a quarter on average in a UK trial of 121 people with Tourette's. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: They Became Pen Pals as Teens, Now 32 Years Later They’re Happily Married
item.description: Two teens who became pen pals on holiday in Kos in 1994 are now happily married. How you can help: Write a letter to an old friend you have lost touch with. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: World-First Bone Marrow Transplant Successfully Treats Non-Malignant Disease
item.description: Doctors performed the first reported bone marrow transplant to treat a non-cancer disease. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: Join a bone marrow donor registry; a cheek swab is usually all it takes. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: San Francisco Gets its Largest-Ever Gift: $100M for Public Parks From Airbnb Founder
item.description: San Francisco received $100 million for its public parks, the largest single gift in city history. How you can help: Join a volunteer day at a park near you. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Vitamin C could help block cancer-linked chemicals in your stomach, study finds
item.description: A model suggests vitamin C with meals may block cancer-linked chemicals forming in the stomach. Evidence: Early research. How you can help: Eat fruit or vegetables rich in vitamin C alongside cured meats. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A simple supplement could help your immune system fight cancer and viral infections
item.description: Rockefeller researchers found arginine helps immune cells fight cancer and viruses in early tests. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Euclid discovers ancient cosmic beacons from the dawn of time, shining like a trillion suns
item.description: The Euclid telescope found 31 ancient quasars, including two record-breakers from the early universe. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: SpaceX successfully catches top of huge Starship rocket for first time
item.description: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket in mid-air for the first time, a step toward reuse. Source: BBC Science & Environment.

item.title: Couple with Autism and ADHD Find Passion Cleaning Filthy Street Signs
item.description: A couple with autism and ADHD found joy in cleaning dirty street signs across their area. How you can help: Pick one small public spot near home and keep it clean. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: Two of the ‘Last Wild Ecosystems’ Untouched by Humans Are Declared New Sanctuaries
item.description: Two remote Pacific atolls with some of the last untouched reefs have been declared sanctuaries. Evidence: Now policy. Source: Good News Network.

item.title: A giant icy world hiding beyond Pluto could be our sixth dwarf planet
item.description: Astronomers found 2026 ED138, a large icy world beyond Pluto that may be a sixth dwarf planet. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Maui Is Becoming a Living Laboratory for Regenerative Tourism
item.description: Maui is asking visitors to help restore land and culture after the 2023 Lahaina fires. Evidence: Trial or pilot. How you can help: When you travel, choose a day of volunteering offered by local groups. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: How two Princeton graduates built the world’s first microplastics removal system
item.description: Two Princeton graduates built a system that removes microplastics at wastewater plants. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: Crows can make decisions twice as fast as humans, scientists discover
item.description: Crows make visual decisions twice as fast as humans, Tübingen researchers found. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
item.description: AI helps predict what a blind man with a brain implant sees, making bionic vision more precise. Evidence: Early research. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: A butterfly that fooled scientists for 200 years finally reveals its secrets
item.description: A common tropical butterfly turned out to be three species, one new to science. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Imagining the Mossy Cities of the Future
item.description: A German startup builds moss walls that clean city air, born from an effort to save one tree. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: After a decade of community pressure, LA bans oil drilling for good
item.description: After a decade of resident pressure, Los Angeles has banned new oil drilling and is phasing out wells. Evidence: Now policy. Source: The Optimist Daily.

item.title: What We’re Reading: An 80-Cent Plastic Bag Is Saving Mothers’ Lives
item.description: A low-cost plastic bag that measures blood loss after birth is helping save mothers' lives. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: NASA’s CHAPEA Mars crew finally emerges after more than a year in isolation
item.description: Four NASA volunteers finished more than a year in a simulated Mars habitat, growing their own food. Source: ScienceDaily.

item.title: Colleges Are Getting Creative to Help Students With Kids
item.description: US colleges are adding childcare, family spaces and support so student parents can finish degrees. Evidence: Trial or pilot. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Spark: When Communities Own the Land, Housing Stays Affordable
item.description: Community land trusts are keeping homes affordable by taking land off the open market. Evidence: Proven at scale. How you can help: Find out if a community land trust works in your area and attend a meeting. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: The Montana Ranch Where Autistic People Are Wranglers and Guides
item.description: A Montana ranch employs autistic adults as guides, wranglers and cooks. Evidence: Proven at scale. Source: Reasons to be Cheerful.

item.title: How to move 1,300 plants for Kew's Palm House mega makeover
item.description: Kew is moving 1,300 plants so its Palm House can be restored. Source: BBC Science & Environment.
